The exuded latex is dried and manipulated to form cakes of uniform composition, variously shaped according to the country of origin, and known in commerce as Turkish, Indian, or European opium. Opium has the properties of opioid analgesics (p.101). Its anal- gesic and sedative actions are due mainly to its content of mor- phine (p.89). It acts less rapidly than morphine since opium ap- pears to be more slowly absorbed; the relaxing action of the papaverine and noscapine on intestinal muscle makes it more constipating than morphine. Opium is intended only as the starting material for the manufac- ture of galenical preparations and is not dispensed as such. It is used as Prepared Opium (Ph. Eur. 6.2), as Powdered Opium (USP 31), as Opium Tincture (BP 2008 or USP 31), or as Cam- phorated Opium Tincture (BP 2008) or Paregoric (USP 31) in various oral preparations. These have included Opiate Squill Linctus (BP 2008) (Gee’s linctus) for cough. Paregoric (USP 31) has been advocated in the USA for the treat- ment of neonatal abstinence syndrome. Abuse.
